$Comment: The skeleton every contract on Old Jack's board inherits through Parent. It is Abstract, so it
is never posted itself.
Season keeps every child out of the draw while Hallow's Eve is off, whatever Requires the child
writes. Listing files each child with the board's contracts. Flow is the quest schema's own group:
AutoTrack pins a contract to the player's quest tracker when they take it at the board, like Old
Jack's quests, if the tracker has room (it holds five and never drops a pin the player chose). A
contract takes no quest-log slot either way. Boards posts a child in the board's night
slots; a contract for the daylight slots, or one drawn more often, writes its own Boards, which
replaces this list whole. Rewards is what every contract on the board pays, through Rewards.Claim
like every contract's: the pay waits at the board until the player collects it. The board leaves
with the event, so a job finished in its last hours waits there until the board is back next
year, which is why the board's own description asks players to collect before Old Jack packs up.
The list is the board's pay table, favor with Old Jack and the Hallowed, and Festival Favor,
which every season's work pays (the Reputation rewards; Amount is how much). A child that writes
its own Rewards.Claim replaces that list whole. Every shipped contract does, to add MMO Skill
Tree's Mmo_Xp row for the skill its work trains, so re-tuning this list means re-tuning theirs
too. That row carries its own Requires, the hytale:mod_installed gate (always Min 1), which leaves
it out on a server without that mod while the plain rows still pay there; a contract whose every
row is gated would pay nothing there, so keep these plain rows. Each bucket inherits on its own, so
a list left in Rewards.Auto here would pay on top of every child's own Claim.
It carries no Requires and no Objectives: a child that writes its own Requires.Factors drops an
inherited gate, and an inherited step can be re-tuned but never removed.
